clues.text: This city lies at the head of a bay on the central coast of Honshu. Honshu is the largest island in this island nation.
clues.narrowing: Rules out inland and small island places; puts the player on the central coast of the largest island.

source.quote: Lying at the head of Tokyo Bay, Tokyo is part of the Kantō region, on the central coast of Honshu, Japan's largest island

clues.text: Summers here are hot and damp, and winters are cool with cold spells at times. Sea storms called typhoons reach this coast in most years.
clues.narrowing: Rules out dry and mild coast lands; keeps a hot, damp summer coast hit by sea storms.

source.quote: with hot, humid summers and cool winters with occasional cold spells

clues.text: In 1603, the Tokugawa rulers made this city their seat of power. It grew from a small fishing village into a vast city.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to the seat chosen by the Tokugawa rulers in 1603.

source.quote: rose to political prominence in 1603 when it became the seat of the Tokugawa shogunate

clues.text: An old castle stands at the heart of this city, and the emperor lives in its grounds today. It became his palace when the court moved here in 1868.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one old castle at the city heart is now the home of an emperor.

source.quote: The former Edo Castle became the new Imperial Palace

clues.text: The emperor and the government of Japan sit in this city. Its law makers meet here in the Diet hall.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the emperor, the government, and the lawmakers all sit in this city.

source.quote: the seat of the Japanese government and the Emperor of Japan

reveal.blurb: Edo was a small fishing village until the Tokugawa rulers made it their seat in 1603, and in 1868 the emperor moved his capital here and gave it a fresh name. Its old castle became the Imperial Palace, and the city grew into a vast port of trains and towers. Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
